# About the Series {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../common/about-series.qmd >}}

# Preface to Volume I {.unnumbered}

Software engineering begins before code and depends on much more than implementation. This volume develops the foundations needed to understand problems, specify requirements, model systems, choose architectures, design usable experiences, organize development work, collaborate through version control, and establish software quality.

The chapters form a practical progression from engineering principles through verified implementation. Examples and projects emphasize professional judgment as well as technique, and the volume can be used as a textbook, course resource, or independent reference.

# How to Use This Volume {.unnumbered}

Read the chapters in sequence for a complete foundation, or use individual chapters as focused references. Learning objectives identify expected outcomes; examples and terminal sessions connect concepts to practice; chapter summaries, key terms, review questions, and exercises support study and instruction.

Volume II extends this foundation into continuous delivery, production infrastructure, security, maintenance, and long-term evolution, but Volume I does not require Volume II for its core use.
